hook.line: Store A: up 60%, then 25% off. Store B: up 20%. Which costs more?
hook.voice: Think you can do this one without touching the hundred and forty? There's a shortcut.

question_voice: Two stores, the same item, different markups and a sale, and we want the gap in price.
signature_move: Turn each percent change into a multiplier.

steps.voice: Turn each change into a multiplier. Up sixty percent is times one point six. Twenty-five off is times point seven five.
Multiply them. One point six times point seven five is one point two.
Store B goes up twenty percent. That's times one point two as well.
Same multiplier on the same cost, so the prices match. We never needed the hundred and forty.

answer.voice: The difference is zero. That's A. Quick check: one forty times one point two is one sixty-eight at both stores.

trap.summary: Subtracting the percents (60 − 25 = 35, more than 20) and concluding Store A charges more, so choosing a nonzero difference.
trap.voice: The trap is subtracting. Sixty minus twenty-five looks like thirty-five, which beats twenty. But the discount comes off the marked-up price, not the original.

check: 140 × 1.2 = 168 at both stores, so the difference is 0.
takeaway: Multiply percent changes; never add or subtract them.
